subject: Grogluk
fact: Grogluk is a 4-foot-tall Duergar with ashen grey skin, scars, tattoos, and a crude clenched-fist pendant, serving the Deepking. He pretends to be alone but is surrounded by invisible and visible guards. His demeanor is defiant and proud, but he demands proof of identity, bribes, and controls access to the city of Gracklstugh.
source_quote: Yes, I do. And are you the Ember Vanguard or are you its prey?

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a Dragonborne whose scales are not red, contradicting the Duergar’s mistaken belief that scale color defines morality. He is falsely implicated in the Ember Vanguard’s wanted poster and carries Stone Guard passes. He is observant, calm under pressure, and recognizes the Duergar’s reliance on magic and propaganda.
source_quote: Then you must not be," and points at the picture of the Ember Vanguard, "the Ember Vanguard.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a perceptive member of the party who recognizes the pattern of despotic Drow and Duergar guards demanding bribes. He is always prepared for contingency, readying spells when others negotiate. He understands the psychology of power and corruption in the Underdark.
source_quote: I have seen so many guards of despotic rulers living among the Drow, and they all want the same thing, a bribe.

subject: Deepking
fact: The Deepking is the ruling sovereign of Gracklstugh, exerting control through Grogluk and a network of guards, propaganda, and fear. His authority is symbolized by the clenched-fist pendant, and he maintains strict identity verification to suppress the Ember Vanguard and maintain order.
source_quote: This Duergar works for the Deepking.

subject: Ember Vanguard
fact: The Ember Vanguard is a wanted group, falsely depicted in Duergar posters with exaggerated and inaccurate features. They are believed to be dangerous revolutionaries, though their true nature is unknown. The Duergar use them as a tool of fear, conflating them with outsiders like the party. Their name is misspelled and their appearance distorted to incite paranoia.
source_quote: The Ember Vanguard, wanted dead as long as we can raise them or aliave.

subject: Derro
fact: The Derro are on edge, exhibiting signs of pre-revolutionary violence. They are oppressed by the Duergar and likely planning rebellion. Their presence is felt in the slums and at the edges of the city, where they watch and wait. They are known to misidentify details, such as the color of scales or the appearance of the Ember Vanguard.
source_quote: The Derro are particularly on edge. If I could express it, it would be a sense of pre-revolutionary violence.

subject: Stone Guard
fact: The Stone Guard is an authoritative organization whose passes are recognized as legitimate but easily forged in the eyes of the Duergar. They are a counterbalance to the Deepking’s power and represent an external legitimacy that Grogluk distrusts but cannot outright deny.
source_quote: I show him the passes of the Stone Guard.

subject: identity verification at West Cleft District
fact: The party undergoes intense scrutiny at the gate to Gracklstugh, where Duergar guards demand proof of identity, inspect weapons, and attempt to classify each member by race and affiliation. The process escalates from questioning to bribery and ritual testing, culminating in Grogluk’s reluctant acceptance after payment and performance of the Bahamut salute.
source_quote: You are a Drow." Turning to Thorin, then Grygum he says, "You are a dwarf and you are an orc!

subject: bribery and passage granted
fact: After Grygum pays Grogluk 20 gold and performs the ritual salute, the guard declares the party cleared to enter. This reveals the corruption at the heart of Duergar governance — authority is for sale, and legitimacy is performative.
source_quote: I size him up and give him 20 gold. He smiles and shouts to the others here that we are to pass through.

subject: Gracklstugh
fact: Gracklstugh is the capital city of the Duergar, ruled by the Deepking. Its outer defenses are heavily guarded, its slums are tense with Derro unrest, and its inner district, Laduguer’s Furrow, is where the wealthiest and most powerful Duergar reside. The city is a fortress of paranoia, propaganda, and magical surveillance.
source_quote: We stand in Laduguer’s Furrow. Here’s where the richest and most powerful of the Duergar live.

subject: West Cleft District
fact: The West Cleft District is the fortified entrance to Gracklstugh, guarded by a newly manned guardhouse that was previously abandoned. It features wanted posters, invisible and visible Duergar sentries, and a gauntlet-like atmosphere where power, politics, and peril converge.
source_quote: This is no mere checkpoint. It’s a gauntlet where power, politics, and peril converge.

subject: Passageway to Grogluk’s chamber
fact: A 10’ wide, 30’ long corridor with 20’ side walls, lined with visible and invisible Duergar guards. It leads to Grogluk’s chamber and demonstrates the Duergar’s use of magic and layered security to intimidate visitors and conceal their true strength.
source_quote: There are at least five more invisible guards we can’t see in this hallway.

subject: clenched-fist pendant
fact: A crude, familiar Underdark token worn by Grogluk, symbolizing loyalty to the Deepking. It is a mark of allegiance used by Duergar enforcers and is recognized by Zalthir as a sign of servitude to the ruling power.
source_quote: It’s a familiar token of the Underdark, a clenched fist that expresses loyalty to the ruler.

subject: wanted poster of the Ember Vanguard
fact: A Duergar propaganda poster depicting the Ember Vanguard with glaring inaccuracies: a red Dragonborne instead of gold, an ancient Drow wizard, and an exaggeratedly fierce Grygum. The poster contains spelling and grammar errors, revealing the Duergar’s ignorance and fear-driven misinformation.
source_quote: The Ember Vanguard, wanted dead as long as we can raise them or aliave.

subject: Grogluk’s hidden agenda
fact: Grogluk’s demand for proof, his acceptance of bribes, and his sudden shift from hostility to compliance suggest he is acting under orders from the Deepking. His true intentions — whether to eliminate the party, recruit them, or test them — remain unclear, and his mention of Grogluk’s superior, Grogluk, implies deeper machinations.
source_quote: Grogluk will wish to speak to you. Follow me.

subject: session date
fact: The events occur during a single session of travel and confrontation in the Underdark, following the party’s recovery of their senses and departure from the Whorlstone caves. The timeline is continuous, with no temporal gaps between encounters.
source_quote: after recovering their senses, to the extent that is possible for the dwarf

subject: Jimjar
fact: Jimjar is smiling as if the goal of the bet was not to win or lose, but to change the group’s mood.
source_quote: Jimjar smiles as if the goal wasn’t to win or lose the bet but something else, to change our mood.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin unbuckled his belt, causing his pants to fall, and laughed along with the group.
source_quote: Thorin takes the bet and accidentally unbuckles his belt, and his pants fall. We all laugh.

subject: Gracklstugh
fact: Gracklstugh is a city of furnaces, bellowing heat, a toxic fog, and haze that blocks out the light; its filth contrasts jarringly with the beauty of Menzoberranzan.
source_quote: Gracklstugh is a city of furnaces, bellowing heat, a toxic fog, and haze that blocks out the light. Visibility is constrained as we move about. The comparison with the filth of Gracklstugh and the beauty of Menzoberranzan is jarring.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz notices another grey-skinned duergar leaning against the wall, eyeing them with cold calculation, and approaches him.
source_quote: As we sneak about, I notice another grey-skinned duergar, leaning against the wall, eyeing us with cold calculation. If something is going to happen, I would rather have a hand in it happening, and so I walk up to him.

subject: Duergar informant
fact: The Duergar informant demands a gold piece and reveals that the Stone Guard is on edge due to the Ember Vanguard’s murder of the Derro High Council.
source_quote: He looks me over and tells us that the Stone Guard is on edge and about strangers in the city. “Any group with a Drow would probably want to be very careful. Everybody’s been on edge since the Ember Vanguard killed several members of the Derro High Council.”

subject: Derro High Council massacre
fact: The Ember Vanguard murdered several members of the Derro High Council, triggering widespread paranoia and destabilizing the power structure of Gracklstugh.
source_quote: The Ember Vanguard killed several members of the Derro High Council.

subject: civil war risk
fact: The death of the Derro High Council members has increased the possibility of a civil war in Gracklstugh, as they were part of the city’s overall power structure.
source_quote: The Derro we killed were not just madmen; they were part of the overall power structure of this city. And with them dead, the possibility of a civil war has suddenly increased.

subject: Hgraam’s Cave
fact: Hgraam’s Cave is the home of stone giants, where a secret ritual once transformed giants into two-headed monsters; the entrance is now closed indefinitely.
source_quote: We end up at Hgraam’s cave and explain to him that there was a secret ritual that was transforming his giants into two-headed monsters. He offers us a small pile of coins. And then asks us to leave, declaring that the entrance to his cavern would be closed for a while.

subject: Hgraam
fact: Hgraam, a stone giant, is skeptical of the surface world and refuses to acknowledge its existence, closing his cavern to outsiders.
source_quote: He scratches his head and says, “I know of no such place. I do not know if such a place even exists. And I would not know what to do with a world that had no stone over my head.”

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir uses his sphere of darkness to conceal the group as they leave Hgraam’s Cave, ensuring safe passage.
source_quote: As we leave Cairngorm’s Cavern, Zalthir uses his sphere of darkness to hide the group. We figure that the haze and darkness will allow us to proceed unmolested.

subject: Gartokkar’s House
fact: Gartokkar’s House is where the group delivers the dragon egg, triggering suspicion and a clerical inquiry due to its occult markings.
source_quote: As we walk through an alley, trying to be inconspicuous, a group of Derro surrounds us. They announce that the Grey Ghosts will have their revenge for the murder of the High Council.

subject: Gartokkar
fact: Gartokkar is pleased when the egg is delivered but becomes worried by its occult markings and seeks the opinion of a cleric of Bahamut.
source_quote: Gartokkar takes the egg and notices the strange occult markings. He is worried. Before I can reassure him further, he turns to Grygum and asks him as a cleric of Bahamut, “What do you think?”

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum, a cleric of Bahamut, dismisses the idea that dragon evil is tied to scale pigmentation but admits he knows little about chromatic dragons beyond their tendency to become evil.
source_quote: Grygum finds the tiresome confusion among the masses that the evil of dragons is a function of scale pigmentation to be very annoying, but sometimes it can be handy. “I am a cleric of the Platinum Dragon. I know much about metallic dragons. But this is a chromatic dragon, and I know very little other than it will become evil.”

subject: egg delivery
fact: The group delivers the dragon egg to Gartokkar under a non-disclosure agreement, receiving a bag of coins in return, though the nature of the deal remains unclear.
source_quote: Gartokkar is pleased. He smiles at me and says, “A deal and a non-disclosure agreement is a deal.” He leaves the main room and comes back with a bag full of coins.

subject: deal with Thermbechaude
fact: The group believes they had a deal with Thermbechaude, but in reality, they never agreed to anything — creating a potential betrayal or misunderstanding.
source_quote: As I walk out, I remember that we had a deal with Thermbechaude. And then I remember, Thermebechaude thought he had an agreement with us. We never had a deal with him.

subject: Gartokkar
fact: Gartokkar warns the group about the Deepking’s agents — shadowy assassins from Menzoberranzan feared even by Stone Guards — and questions how they survived them.
source_quote: I heard the Deepking’s agents are everywhere, looking for a mercenary band so fierce that the Stone Guards are afraid to face them head-on. They are not mere adventurers, more like shadowy assassins from Menzoberranzan with powerful magic and blades that can rend souls. How did you manage to survive them?

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin responds to Gartokkar’s warning by claiming the group appeared small and insignificant, successfully deflecting suspicion.
source_quote: “We appeared small and insignificant.”

subject: Derro ambush
fact: A group of Derro ambushes the party, blaming them for the murder of the High Council and demanding revenge for the Grey Ghosts.
source_quote: As we walk through an alley, trying to be inconspicuous, a group of Derro surrounds us. They announce that the Grey Ghosts will have their revenge for the murder of the High Council.

subject: Derro massacre
fact: The party kills five Derro in self-defense, uncovering a note that falsely identifies them as the Ember Vanguard.
source_quote: A few moments later, there are five dead Derro. As I pick through the coins in their pocket, I find a note.

subject: note from Derro
fact: The note falsely identifies the party as the Ember Vanguard, accuses them of murdering the Derro High Council, stealing the Egg, and orders the Grey Ghosts to stalk, strike from shadows, and recover the Egg.
source_quote: To all - The Deepking’s agents—the four shadows, The Ember Vanguard, who walk among us, wielding dark magic and unmatched skill—have brought death and dishonor to our kin. They are the ones who crushed our leader and stole what is rightfully ours: The Egg. Your mission is clear: Stalk them relentlessly... Strike from the shadows... Leave paranoia in their wake... Recover The Egg. It belongs to the Gray Ghosts.

subject: Ember Vanguard misidentification
fact: The party is being falsely labeled as the Ember Vanguard by the Grey Ghosts, creating a dangerous misconception that could lead to widespread pursuit.
source_quote: The note falsely identifies the party as the Ember Vanguard, accusing them of murdering the Derro High Council and stealing the Egg.

subject: Darklake
fact: The group heads toward the Darklake after the ambush, carrying the weight of false accusations and rising tension across Gracklstugh.
source_quote: With this warning, we head out towards the Darklake.

subject: Grey Ghosts
fact: The Grey Ghosts are a vengeful Derro faction seeking to recover the Egg and punish those they believe are the Ember Vanguard, using stealth, paranoia, and assassination.
source_quote: They announce that the Grey Ghosts will have their revenge for the murder of the High Council.

subject: Ember Vanguard
fact: The Ember Vanguard are real assassins who murdered the Derro High Council and stole the Egg, but the party is being falsely blamed for their actions.
source_quote: The Deepking’s agents—the four shadows, The Ember Vanguard, who walk among us, wielding dark magic and unmatched skill—have brought death and dishonor to our kin. They are the ones who crushed our leader and stole what is rightfully ours: The Egg.

subject: Deepking’s agents
fact: The Deepking’s agents are shadowy assassins feared by the Stone Guards, possibly identical to the Ember Vanguard, and are now actively hunting the party.
source_quote: I heard the Deepking’s agents are everywhere, looking for a mercenary band so fierce that the Stone Guards are afraid to face them head-on. They are not mere adventurers, more like shadowy assassins from Menzoberranzan with powerful magic and blades that can rend souls.

subject: egg’s origin
fact: The origin and true nature of the dragon egg remain mysterious, its occult markings suggesting a ritualistic or forbidden creation, and its viability uncertain.
source_quote: Gartokkar takes the egg and notices the strange occult markings. He is worried. We rescued it from a mysterious ritual.

subject: fallen leader's vengeance
fact: The dead do not rest, and neither do those who seek vengeance for the fallen leader; death follows the trespassers who believe they can outrun shadows.
source_quote: This is not merely an order; it is a cold, cruel vendetta for our fallen leader. You carry death with you for these trespassers. They believe they can outrun shadows, but the dead do not rest, and neither do we.

subject: shadow swallowing
fact: Failure is not an option; those who do not yield to the shadows must become them — a mandate of absolute annihilation.
source_quote: Failure is not an option. Be swallowed by the shadows, or make them so.
